revealWordProblem.title: (Review from 10.5) Apply: The Louvre Pyramid
revealWordProblem.text: The Louvre Pyramid in Paris is a square pyramid made of glass panels. How could you use a net and the surface area formula to find the total area of glass in its four triangular faces?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Unfold the pyramid into a net: the square base separates from the four triangular faces so each one lies flat and can be measured on its own. Since the question only asks about the glass in the four triangular faces, find the area of one triangular face using ½ × base edge × slant height, then multiply by 4 — the base square is not part of this total. For example, if the base edge is 6 ft and the slant height is 8 ft, one triangular face is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 ft², so the four faces together need 4 × 24 = 96 ft² of glass.

turnAndTalk.question: A square pyramid time capsule display has a square base and four triangular faces that meet at a point on top. To find its surface area, which parts do you need to measure?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Surface area of a pyramid is the base area plus the areas of all the triangular lateral faces.

stems.en: I need the area of the ___ plus the areas of the ___ triangular faces.
stems.es: Necesito el área de la ___ más las áreas de las ___ caras triangulares.

stems.en: The surface area is the ___ area plus the ___ faces.
stems.es: El área de superficie es el área de la ___ más las caras ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain a square pyramid's surface area = base area + the four triangular lateral faces, and that you add every face together.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why do you use the slant height, not the pyramid's vertical height, to find the area of each triangular face?
extendStems: I use the slant height because it is the ___ of each triangular face.
The vertical height would not work because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: For Display A (square base 6×6, slant height 8), how did you combine the base area and the four triangular faces to get the total surface area?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Add the base area to four times the area of one triangular face (½ × base × slant height).

stems.en: The base area is ___ × ___ = ___, and one triangular face is ½ × 6 × 8 = ___.
stems.es: El área de la base es ___ × ___ = ___, y una cara triangular es ½ × 6 × 8 = ___.

stems.en: The total surface area is the base plus 4 × ___ = ___ in².
stems.es: El área total de superficie es la base más 4 × ___ = ___ in².

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute base = 36 in², one face = 24 in², four faces = 96 in², total SA = 132 in², distinguishing base from lateral faces.
turnAndTalk.extend: Two pyramids have the same 8×8 base but different slant heights. How will their surface areas compare, and which part stays the same?
extendStems: The pyramid with the larger slant height has ___ surface area because ___.
The ___ area stays the same because slant height only affects ___.

turnAndTalk.question: A museum builds a square pyramid display case with base edge 3 ft and slant height 4 ft, and the base is open (no glass). Talk through how to find how much glass the 4 triangular sides need.
turnAndTalk.kernel: Find one triangular face area, multiply by 4, and skip the base since it is open.

stems.en: Each triangular face has area ½ × ___ × ___ = ___ ft².
stems.es: Cada cara triangular tiene área ½ × ___ × ___ = ___ ft².

stems.en: Four faces need ___ ft² of glass, and the base needs ___ because it is open.
stems.es: Cuatro caras necesitan ___ ft² de vidrio, y la base necesita ___ porque está abierta.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute one face = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft², four faces = 24 ft², and explain the open base is not counted, so only the lateral area matters.
turnAndTalk.extend: How does leaving the base open change which formula you use, and how would the answer change if the base needed glass too?
extendStems: Leaving the base open means I use only the ___ area because ___.
If the base needed glass, I would add ___ to the total.

turnAndTalk.question: A classmate found a square pyramid's surface area by adding only the four triangular faces. What did they forget, and how would you correct it?
turnAndTalk.kernel: They left out the base area, which must be added to the lateral faces for total surface area.

stems.en: They forgot to add the ___ area to the triangular faces.
stems.es: Olvidaron sumar el área de la ___ a las caras triangulares.

stems.en: The correct total surface area is the base plus the ___ lateral faces.
stems.es: El área de superficie total correcta es la base más las ___ caras laterales.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students identify the missing base area and state that total surface area = base area + all lateral (triangular) faces.
turnAndTalk.extend: When is it correct to leave out the base (like an open display case), and when must it be included? Generalize a rule.
extendStems: You leave out the base when ___, but include it when ___.
In general, total surface area of a pyramid is always ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Surface Area of Pyramids, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Surface area of a pyramid = base area + the area of all the triangular lateral faces.

stems.en: When a problem felt tricky, I ___ first because ___.
stems.es: Cuando un problema se sentía difícil, primero ___ porque ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.GR.4 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

optional.stem: (Lesson 10.4) A rectangular time capsule box measures 3 in by 4 in by 5 in. How much wrapping paper covers its surface (no overlap)?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area needs the sum of all six face areas, not length × width × height.
You found the sum of three face areas but forgot each face has a matching opposite one.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.

optional.stem: (Lesson 10.5) Your first gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 7 in and a slant height of 9 in. How much wrapping paper (total surface area) covers it?
optional.explanation: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². SA = 49 + 126 = 175 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
choiceFeedback: You found the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base.
Recalculate the base area (side × side) and each triangular face separately before adding.
Check the units — wrapping paper covers a surface, so it needs square units, not cubic.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.4) What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area adds up all six face areas instead of multiplying three edges.
Check the units — a surface measurement needs square units, not cubic.
You found half the faces — remember each face has a matching opposite face to double.
hints: You need surface area — the total of all 6 face areas of the 5 × 4 × 3 prism — not the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: three different faces, each with a matching twin on the opposite side.
Find the three face areas first: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each, then add the results.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.4) How many faces does a triangular prism have?
approaching.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.
choiceFeedback: Count again — a triangular prism has more rectangular sides than that, plus its two ends.
That's the face count for a rectangular prism — a triangular prism has one fewer face.
That's just the rectangular sides — don't forget the two triangular ends.
hints: Picture a tent or a triangular chocolate box: two triangle ends plus rectangles wrapping around the sides.
Count the two triangular bases first, then count one rectangle for each side of the triangle.
A triangle has 3 sides, so count 3 rectangular faces. Then add the triangular ends to that count.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.5) A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
approaching.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
choiceFeedback: You calculated the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
Recheck each triangular face area — make sure you take half of base times slant height for each.
hints: A square pyramid has TWO kinds of faces: one square base (5 × 5) and four identical triangles with slant height 7.
SA = base area + 4 triangle areas, where each triangle is ½ × base edge × slant height.
Base first: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Then one triangle: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiply that by 4 and add the base area.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.5) How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
approaching.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.
choiceFeedback: A square base has four sides — count a triangular face for each side of the square.
The square base isn't a lateral (triangular) face — only count the slanted triangle sides.
That's too many — count only the slanted triangular sides around the square base.
hints: Lateral faces are the slanted triangles on the sides — the square base itself doesn't count.
Each side of the square base holds up exactly one triangle. Count the sides of a square.
Trace the base: it's a square. Count one triangle leaning against each side of that square.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 10.4) Calculate the surface area of each rectangular prism time capsule.
onLevel.hint: Use the formula V = length × width × height for each row.
hints: Each capsule needs SURFACE AREA: the sum of all six face areas, written in square units.
Row by row, use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh — double each of the three different faces, then add.
Capsule E: the faces are 12×8 = 96, 12×5 = 60, and 8×5 = 40. Double each, then add the three results.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.4) A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
onLevel.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
choiceFeedback: You added the three rectangular faces but left out the two triangular bases.
You added the two slanted rectangular faces and the bases but missed the bottom rectangular face.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Gather the parts: two triangle bases (base 6 in, height 4 in) and three rectangles, each 10 in long.
SA = 2 triangle areas + 3 rectangle areas. Each rectangle is one triangle side (6, 5, or 5) times the 10 in length.
Triangles first: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, doubled is 24 in². Then find the rectangles: 6 × 10, 5 × 10, and 5 × 10.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 10.5) Find the surface area of each square pyramid.
onLevel.hint: Use the formula V = length × width × height for each row.
hints: Each row needs two answers: the square base's area, then the TOTAL surface area (base + 4 triangles).
Base area = edge × edge. Then add 4 × (½ × edge × slant height) for the four triangular faces.
Pyramid X: base area is 12 × 12. Each triangle is ½ × 12 × 10 — find that, multiply by 4, and add to the base.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.5) A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
onLevel.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
choiceFeedback: That's just the lateral area — add the base area too for total surface area.
That's just the base area — add the lateral (triangular) area too for the total.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Both pieces are already given: base area 49 cm² and lateral (triangle) area 84 cm².
Total surface area = base area + lateral area — one addition, keeping square units.
Set up the sum 49 + 84 and add carefully, keeping cm² in your answer.

extending.title: (Lesson 10.4) Find the Surface Area Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Rectangular prism: l = 12 cm, w = 7 cm, h = 5 cm

extending.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply 7 × 5 by 2. It should be 2(7×5) = 2(35) = 70, not 35. Correct: SA = 168 + 120 + 70 = 358 cm².
hints: Check Step 3: did the student multiply every face pair by 2?
2(7×5) = 2(35) = 70, not 35. The student forgot the '2' on the last pair.

extending.title: (Lesson 10.5) Find the Surface Area Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 10 in, slant height = 8 in

workedExample.label: Lateral Area
workedExample.work: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (one face). Total lateral = 40 × 3 = 120 in²

extending.correctWork: A square pyramid has 4 lateral faces, not 3. Total lateral = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correct: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
hints: Check Step 3: how many lateral faces does a square pyramid have?
A square base has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangular faces. The student only multiplied by 3.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Pyramids is finding the four triangular lateral faces correctly (½ × base edge × slant height, times 4) and then stopping — forgetting to add the base area at the end. This leaves the total surface area too small by exactly the base's area. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I add the base area to the four lateral faces, or did I stop after the sides?'

connect.scenario: A museum is building a square pyramid display case. The base edge is 3 feet and the slant height is 4 feet. The glass costs $12 per square foot.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the glass for all 4 triangular sides cost? (The base is open — no glass needed.)
connect.prompt: Each triangular face has area = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___ ft². Four faces: 4 × ___ = ___ ft². Cost: ___ × $12 = $___.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 10.4) A rectangular prism has l = 8 ft, w = 6 ft, h = 3 ft. What is the surface area?
exitTicket.explanation: SA = 2(8×6) + 2(8×3) + 2(6×3) = 96 + 48 + 36 = 180 ft². Surface area uses square units (ft²).
choiceFeedback: 144 is the volume — surface area sums all six faces.
Surface area uses square units (ft²), not cubic.
You found only three faces — each face has a matching pair.
hints: You want the surface area of an 8 × 6 × 3 prism: all six faces added, in square units (ft²).
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh — three different face areas, each counted twice.
Faces first: 8×6 = 48, 8×3 = 24, and 6×3 = 18. Double each area, then add the three results.
